- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward → reduce forecast dip depth or add slight upward bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots downward → cap forecast decline or add 1–2% upward adjustment.
- If model forecast mean is significantly above true outcome mean (e.g., >+3% over 30d), apply downward bias proportional to sentiment magnitude (e.g., -0.1x sentiment value).
- If sentiment turns positive after negative streak, model often underreacts → increase forecast slope or add 0.5–1.0% upward bias.
- For 30d horizon, model tends to overestimate early-term decline (first 5–7 days) → reduce forecast drop in first 5 days if sentiment is negative.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often underestimates mean reversion → add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to mid-term forecast.
- When sentiment is volatile (±0.3 or more), model overfits short-term noise → smooth forecast curve with 3–5 day moving average filter.
